question: Do observed label renamings select a generalizing program, and does one frozen crossing reduce work to certify a correct return?
inputs: Training tuples and bits, ordinary reversible instructions and one optional previously learned crossing. A separate verifier owns the ten full target tables.
forbidden_inputs: Task identifiers, formulas, actual symmetry, held labels, and witness programs as selector or search inputs. No verification failure details in fitting.
mapping: Evaluate one task-fitted renaming rule and two blind controls on the same candidates. Deploy independent, timed, certified shortest, fitted-renaming and direct checking on matched search streams.
primary_observable: Single-choice exact held success, pairwise choice on tied training programs, exact verified returns, total work including failures, certification and acquisition.
comparators_or_controls: Shortest, unconditional renaming, direct verification, equal-training opposite-answer pair, expansion of every crossing, complete finite truth tables.
resource_budget: Ten fresh predicates, three paired seeds, 49,184 proposals per stream, three deployable policies, six fixed checkpoints with at most four requests each in ranked arms.
first_executable_signal: Two indistinguishable training sets permit different completions. Fitted renaming may distinguish other cases.
stop_rule: Finish the specified panel, retaining all censored outcomes and blind errors.
